title: 01. Empty Board & Opening (30k–28k)
description: Learn where to place your first stones on a 9x9 board: center influence, 3-3/3-4 corners, and avoiding slow 1st-line edges.

puzzles.title: First Stone on a Blank 9x9
puzzles.prompt: Blank 9x9 board. Play the highest-influence opening move that radiates power in all four directions.

solutions.feedback: Correct! E5 (Tengen) sits at the exact center of the 9x9 board, radiating influence toward every corner and side.
Solid! The 3-3 star point immediately secures corner territory on a 9x9 board.

wrongHints.default: Too close to the edge or off-balance. On Move 1, claim the center (E5) or a 3-3 corner star point (C3, C7, G3, G7) where stones surround territory efficiently.

puzzles.title: Claiming an Open Corner
puzzles.prompt: White opened at E5. Claim a 3-3 corner point to build a secure base of territory.

solutions.feedback: Great! C3 stakes out the bottom-left corner cleanly instead of bumping head-on into White's center stone.
Great! G7 stakes out the top-right corner cleanly.
Great! C7 stakes out the top-left corner cleanly.
Great! G3 stakes out the bottom-right corner cleanly.

wrongHints.default: Avoid attaching directly to White's center stone or crawling on the 1st/2nd line. Step into one of the four 3-3 corner star points (C3, C7, G3, G7).

puzzles.title: The 3rd Line vs. 1st Line Rule
puzzles.prompt: Black has C3 and White has G7. Extend along the 3rd line to build side territory without crawling on the edge.

solutions.feedback: Textbook 3rd-line extension! F3 builds a two-space wall along the bottom while aiming at the bottom-right corner.
Textbook 3rd-line extension! C6 builds a two-space wall along the left side.
Strong! Taking the center E5 links your corner stone to the rest of the board.

wrongHints.default: 1st and 2nd line moves only secure 1 point per stone. Extend two spaces along the 3rd line (F3 or C6) or take the center (E5).
